Cta.title: Ship an editor in five minutes
Cta.text: Install, load the stylesheet, mount. Free and open source under the MIT license: no license key, no telemetry, no cloud service.

stats.label: The core plus a ready-made package for every major framework
Checked with axe-core in every release

Features.title: Everything you need to write, built in
Features.description: And the things your users, your security team and your auditors ask for.

items.title: Accessible, WCAG 2.2
items.text: Fully keyboard operable with no trap, screen reader announcements, Windows High Contrast, reduced motion and a dark theme. Checked with axe-core on every release.

items.title: Your brand, in one color
items.text: Set ui.brand and the buttons, links, focus ring and selection follow, in light and dark. Every button has its own tokens, so the editor fits any brand and any dashboard theme.

items.title: Secure by default
items.text: DOMPurify on every input, a URL allow-list, Trusted Types and no unsafe-inline. It runs under a strict CSP.

items.title: RTL and Arabic, first-class
items.text: English and Arabic built in, and you can add your own. The whole UI mirrors in RTL and every block has dir="auto".

items.title: Form-ready web component
items.text: '<'owe-editor name'>' takes part in plain HTML forms, so a form post, htmx or Turbo works with no glue code.

items.title: Small and tree-shakable
items.text: The whole editor, sanitizer and UI come to about 133 kB gzipped. Framework wrappers add around 1 kB.

items.title: Headless when you need it
items.text: Use the full UI, or ui: false and open-wysiwyg-editor/headless for your own. Add toolbar buttons and write extensions.

items.title: Built on ProseMirror
items.text: A strict document schema, transactions and undo history from ProseMirror, the proven toolkit for rich text editing.

Footer.about: An accessible, RTL-first rich text editor for every framework. MIT licensed, with no license key and no telemetry.

Hero.title: A rich text editor that works everywhere.
Hero.sub: Accessible, RTL-first and safe under a strict CSP. One small core and a ready-made package for every framework, from plain HTML forms to Next.js.

Install.title: Up and running in three steps
Install.description: Install the core package, load the stylesheet and mount an editor. Using a framework? Its package does these steps for you.

steps.title: Install
steps.text: Use your package manager, or load one script from a CDN with no build step.

steps.title: Load the styles
steps.text: Load the stylesheet once. It styles the editor, its UI and its content. Your page's CSS, Tailwind included, doesn't change how the editor looks: theme it with its tokens.

steps.title: Render the editor
steps.text: createEditor(options) mounts the editor in the element you pass and returns an editor. Call it in the browser, after the element exists.

Install.saveText: Read the clean, sanitized HTML (or ProseMirror JSON) and load it back later.
Install.showText: On a page with no editor, load content.css and wrap the sanitized HTML in owe-content-root.
Install.serverNote: The browser is not a security boundary. Sanitize the HTML again on the server before you store it.
Install.frameworkText: Install its package instead of the core. It brings the core with it and re-exports the whole API. <link>Pick your framework</link>

Api.title: Everything the core exports
Api.description: One page of options, methods and attributes. The framework packages re-export all of it.

options.title: createEditor(options)
options.description: Every option, with its default. All of them are optional.

ui.title: ui options
ui.description: The built-in toolbar, status bar and theme. Pass false instead for a headless editor.

callbacks.title: Callbacks
callbacks.description: Pass them as options. The framework packages always call the latest function.

commands.title: Commands
commands.description: Run them with editor.commands.name(), test them with editor.can().name() and combine them with editor.chain()…run().

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.description: placeholder, readonly, disabled, dir, content-lang and label follow later changes. value, language and toolbar are read when the editor starts.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Set options before the element is added to the page.

events.title: Events
events.description: Both bubble, so you can listen on the form.

entries.title: Entry points
entries.description: What each import path gives you.

options.element: Container, CSS selector or textarea (hidden and kept in sync). Omit it to create the editor detached and append editor.root yourself.
options.content: Initial content: HTML (always sanitized) or ProseMirror JSON.
options.placeholder: Text shown when the editor is empty.
options.ariaLabel: Accessible name and description of the editing area.
options.contentLang: lang of the content, used for spellcheck and screen readers.
options.urlPolicy: '{' protocols, allowDataImages, allowRelative '}'. Allowed link and image URLs.
options.ui: Toolbar, custom items, status bar, theme and shortcuts. false = headless.

ui.toolbar: Item names and "|" separators. false hides the toolbar.
ui.items: Custom or overriding toolbar buttons, referenced by name in toolbar.
ui.statusbar: Status bar content. characterCount can take '{' limit '}'.
ui.stickyToolbar: Keep the toolbar visible while scrolling long documents.
ui.shortcuts: Key bindings of the built-in UI.

callbacks.onFocus: The editing area gained or lost focus.

methods.getText: Plain text. Blocks are separated by \n\n by default.
methods.setContent: Load HTML or JSON. emitUpdate and addToHistory are off by default.
methods.chain: Several commands in one transaction and one undo step.
methods.isActive: Is a mark or node active, e.g. isActive("heading", '{' level: 2 '}').
methods.getAttributes: Attributes at the selection, e.g. a link''s href.
methods.on: Listen to an editor event. Returns an unsubscribe function.
methods.subscribe: Store-style subscription that fires on every change.
methods.announce: Send a message to screen readers.
methods.destroy: Remove the editor and its listeners.

attributes.name: Form field name. The form submits the editor''s HTML under it.
attributes.disabled: Disables the editor and leaves it out of the form.
attributes.content: lang of the content (spellcheck and screen readers).
attributes.label: Accessible name. Or point a '<'label for'>' at the element''s id.
attributes.value: Initial content as HTML. Read once, when the editor is created.
attributes.language: UI language, e.g. ar. Read once. Defaults to '<'html lang'>'.
attributes.toolbar: Toolbar items separated by spaces ("bold italic | link"), or none. Read once.

properties.editor: The live editor, or null while the element is not in the document.
properties.value: The content as HTML. Setting it loads new content.
properties.options: More createEditor() options. Set it before the element is added to the page. Attributes win over it.

events.input: On every change. event.target.value has the HTML.
events.change: When the editor loses focus after a change.

entries.core: The engine, every extension and the accessible UI.
entries.headless: The engine and extensions without UI code.
entries.contentCss: Content styles only, for pages that display saved HTML (also content.min.css).
entries.globalJs: A script tag build. Exposes window.OpenWysiwygEditor and defines '<'owe-editor'>'.

Frameworks.title: Pick your framework
Frameworks.description: Each package re-exports the whole core API and ships the stylesheets. Install one and you are done.
Frameworks.security: The editor sanitizes what it loads and produces, but that is not a security boundary: anyone can post any string to your API. Sanitize the HTML again with a library you trust before you store it or render it for other users.

react.name: React
react.blurb: RichTextEditor and useEditor() for React 18+, Remix, Gatsby and Vite.
notes: SSR-safe: the server renders an empty container and the hidden input, and the editor starts in the browser.
value is loaded only when it differs from the HTML the editor last produced, so typing never moves the cursor.
Callbacks and the runtime options (editable, placeholder, aria*, dir, contentLang) follow every render. Everything else is read at mount: give the component a new key to change it.

next.name: Next.js
next.blurb: The React package with a "use client" banner. Use it straight from Server Components and wire it to Server Actions with name.
notes: Import the stylesheet once, in app/layout.tsx (or pages/_app.tsx).
A Server Component cannot pass functions such as onChange. Use a client component for those, or use name with a Server Action.
You do not need dynamic(…, '{' ssr: false '}'): nothing touches window or document while rendering.

preact.name: Preact
preact.blurb: The same API as the React package, on preact/hooks. Use class instead of className.
notes: Props and options are the same as in the React package, with class for the wrapper.
SSR-safe: the server renders an empty container and the hidden input.

vue.name: Vue
vue.blurb: A v-model component for Vue 3.3+. Safe for server-side rendering.
notes: options takes everything createEditor() accepts except element. Callbacks and runtime options follow changes; the rest is read at mount, so remount with a new :key.
The editor starts in onMounted, so it works in Nuxt and Vite SSR without '<'ClientOnly'>'.
Events: update:modelValue (HTML) and ready (the editor). A template ref exposes editor.

nuxt.name: Nuxt
nuxt.blurb: A Nuxt module. It auto-imports '<'RichTextEditor'>' and adds the stylesheet. The component itself comes from the Vue package.
notes: No import and no '<'ClientOnly'>': the server renders an empty container and the editor starts in the browser.
Set css: false to import the stylesheet yourself. Props, events and options are the Vue package''s.

angular.name: Angular
angular.blurb: A standalone component with ngModel and reactive forms support. It starts in the browser only and runs outside the zone.
notes: Inputs: value (two-way), options, placeholder, readonly. Outputs: valueChange, ready.
The control is marked touched on blur, and disable() makes the editor read-only.
It starts in afterNextRender, so it works with Angular SSR and hydration.

svelte.name: Svelte
svelte.blurb: A use:richText action for Svelte 3, 4 and 5. Actions never run on the server, so it is safe in SvelteKit.
notes: content goes in and onUpdate sends the HTML back. Outside changes load into the editor; its own HTML is not reloaded, so the cursor stays.
Pass any editor option except element. Runtime options apply live; the rest is read when the editor is created (wrap the element in '{'#key …'}' to recreate it).

solid.name: Solid
solid.blurb: A use:richText directive for Solid 1.6+ and SolidStart. The object you pass is read reactively.
notes: Keep the richText; line. TypeScript and Babel drop imports that look unused, and use:richText is only a reference to the function.
Directives only run in the browser, so there is nothing to guard with isServer.

astro.name: Astro
astro.blurb: An .astro component that renders '<'owe-editor'>'. It works with plain form posts and needs no UI framework.
notes: The component imports its own script and styles, so there is nothing else to add.
The server renders only the '<'owe-editor'>' element, with the initial HTML in an escaped value attribute. The field works with a plain form post in static and server output.

web-component.name: Web component
web-component.blurb: '<'owe-editor'>' is the full editor as an HTML tag. It is a form-associated custom element in the light DOM, so there is no Shadow DOM and it is CSP-safe.
notes: The form submits the editor''s HTML under name, and form.reset() restores the starting content. A '<'label for'>' pointing at its id becomes the accessible name.
Use the value attribute or a '<'template'>' child when the content comes from users: neither can run anything before the editor sanitizes it.

vanilla.name: Vanilla JS
vanilla.blurb: The core is one function, createEditor(options). Use it with any bundler, or from a CDN with one script tag.
notes: Load the stylesheet once, call createEditor() in the browser after the element exists (it throws during server-side rendering), and call editor.destroy() when the element goes away.
On a '<'textarea'>' the editor hides the field and keeps its value in sync. The textarea''s '<'label'>' becomes the editor''s accessible name.

others.name: Lit, Alpine, htmx…
others.blurb: Anything that can print HTML can use the '<'owe-editor'>' tag: Lit, Alpine.js, htmx, Turbo, Ember, Qwik, WordPress and PHP. It fires input and change and takes part in forms.
notes: Load the CDN script and stylesheet once (or import open-wysiwyg-editor/element and style.css), then put the tag in your markup.
In Qwik, import the element inside a visible task so it never runs on the server. In WordPress, esc_attr() keeps user content from breaking out of the attribute.

Guides.title: Ship it with confidence
Guides.description: Accessibility, security, styling, theming and languages: the five things teams ask about before they ship an editor. Open one to read more.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.summary: WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard shortcuts and the patterns it follows.
a11y.intro: The editor targets WCAG 2.2 AA, ATAG 2.0 and WAI-ARIA authoring practices, and is checked with axe-core on every release.
shortcuts: Return from the toolbar to the text
Open the list of keyboard shortcuts

patterns.text: The ARIA toolbar pattern with one tab stop and a roving tabindex. Arrow keys, Home and End move between buttons, and the arrows follow the RTL direction. Buttons announce their pressed state and their shortcuts.
Menus follow the APG menu-button pattern. Dialogs are native '<'dialog'>' elements with labelled fields, inline error messages and focus returned to where you were.
In the text, Tab indents lists and moves between table cells. Press Esc and then Tab to leave the editor.
Live regions announce results such as “2 of 5 matches” and “Link inserted”. editor.announce() sends your own messages.

Focus is always visible. Windows High Contrast (forced-colors) and prefers-reduced-motion are honored, and there is a dark theme. At narrow widths and 400% zoom the toolbar wraps instead of scrolling sideways.
Images prompt for alt text and offer a decorative option, tables get headers and a caption by default, and color pickers report contrast and warn below AA.

a11y.tip: Give each editor an accessible name: a '<'label for'>' on a textarea or '<'owe-editor'>', or ariaLabel / ariaLabelledBy. Use ariaDescribedBy for help text, set contentLang for content in another language, and put lang and dir on the content you display from storage.

security.title: Security
security.summary: Strict CSP, Trusted Types and what to do on the server.
security.intro: The editor works under a strict Content Security Policy with Trusted Types. This site itself runs under that policy.

layers.name: Input
layers.text: Every input path (initial content, setContent, paste, drop, source view) passes through DOMPurify. Script-capable elements are removed before parsing.

layers.name: Model
layers.text: Only schema-known content survives, unless HtmlSupport is added, and even then its blocklist applies.

layers.name: Output
layers.text: getHTML() is produced by a serializer that does not use the DOM. It validates tag and attribute names, escapes every value and checks every URL again.

layers.name: URLs
layers.text: Allowed by default: http, https, mailto and tel, plus relative URLs. data: images are off unless urlPolicy.allowDataImages is set.

layers.name: CSP
layers.text: Works under script-src ''self''; style-src ''self''; require-trusted-types-for ''script''. The live view never writes inline style strings.

layers.name: Trusted Types
layers.text: Adds one policy named open-wysiwyg-editor to your trusted-types directive, or pass your own with setTrustedTypesPolicy().

security.csp: Add the editor''s policy name to trusted-types. Paste handling also uses ProseMirror''s ProseMirrorClipboard policy, so list that one too.
security.tt: With require-trusted-types-for ''script'', every HTML sink needs a trusted value. The editor creates one policy and uses it everywhere.
security.serverTitle: The browser is not a security boundary
security.server: Never trust HTML that comes from the client. The editor cleans what it loads and produces, but anyone can post any string to your API. Sanitize again on the server, with a library you trust, before you store or render it for other users.
security.serverNote: For initial content from users, use the value attribute or a '<'template'>' child on '<'owe-editor'>', never raw children. Neither can run anything before the editor sanitizes it.
security.report: Found a vulnerability? Please report it privately, see the <link>security policy</link>.

styling.title: Styling
styling.summary: Cascade layers, the --owe-* design tokens and light and dark themes.
styling.intro: The editor is isolated from your page's CSS: resets, element rules and utility classes don't reach into it, and only a more specific selector or !important overrides its rules. Theme the editor by setting design tokens.
styling.files: open-wysiwyg-editor/style.css has the editor, its UI and its content styles. content.css has only the content styles, for published pages: wrap the saved HTML in '<'div class="owe-content-root"'>'. Each framework package ships the same files under its own name, for example @open-wysiwyg-editor/vue/style.css.
styling.tokens: Set tokens on .owe (or :root). This site themes the editor like this:
tokenRows: Corner radius of the editor and its controls.
Backgrounds of the content area, the toolbar and panels.
Borders. Keep --owe-border at 3:1 against the background.
The one brand color, the second color of the gradient edge, and the text on brand fills. See the Theming guide.
Derived from the brand: links and text, the fill of pressed buttons, and the focus ring.
styling.theme: The editor ships a light and a dark token set. Set ui.theme to light, dark or auto (the default, which follows the system), and override tokens under .owe[data-theme="dark"] for different values per theme.

theming.title: Theming and brand colors
theming.summary: One brand color, button tokens, and recipes for shadcn/ui and your own dashboard.
theming.intro: Set one color and the whole editor follows it, in light and dark: pressed toolbar buttons, dialog buttons, links, the focus ring, the caret, the text selection and the gradient edge of the card. Try it with the brand color in the playground on the home page.
theming.one: ui.brand takes any CSS color and picks black or white for the text on brand buttons by contrast. The brand attribute does the same on '<'owe-editor'>'. In plain CSS, set --owe-brand (and --owe-on-brand if white does not read well) on .owe, on a wrapper or on :root.
theming.derived: Everything else comes from the brand with color-mix(). Set any of these yourself and yours wins.
derivedRows: The brand. Pressed toolbar buttons and primary dialog buttons.
The primary color mixed 15% toward black.
Link and text color: the brand mixed 30% toward black in light, 40% toward white in dark.
The brand at 22% opacity in light, 45% in dark.
From --owe-brand to --owe-brand-2. ui.brand sets a lighter tint as the second color.
theming.buttons: These restyle the buttons, the toolbar and the card without touching a selector. Set them on .owe or on any element around it, such as your dashboard wrapper. Unset, they use the default shown.
buttonRows: The primary button in dialogs (Insert, Apply).
Corners of buttons and menu items.
Toolbar, find bar and status bar.
Border and corners of the card.
theming.buttonsExample: A dark toolbar over a light editing area, with smaller corners:
theming.dashboard: Point the tokens at the variables your design system already defines, for example shadcn/ui as below. The editor never declares a token itself, so yours wins wherever you set it, and the tokens read your variables when they are used, so the editor follows your light and dark themes without a script. Also set theme to dark when your dashboard is dark, so links, selection and native controls match.
theming.later: '<'owe-editor'>' follows changes to its theme and brand attributes. For createEditor(), call setTheme() on its UI. It replaces the whole theme, so pass everything you want to keep. The playground on the home page does exactly this.
theming.contrast: The editor cannot choose colors for you. --owe-accent keeps 4.5:1 on white for typical brands, but a very pale brand needs an explicit --owe-accent, and pressed buttons need 3:1 against the toolbar.

languages.title: Languages and RTL
languages.summary: English and Arabic built in, your own languages, and right-to-left content.
languages.intro: English and Arabic are built in. The UI mirrors itself in RTL languages, and every block in the content picks its own direction.
languages.arabic: Set language for the interface and dir for the base direction of the content. Without dir, each text block gets dir="auto", so Arabic and English paragraphs each display correctly in the same document. Word and character counts segment words correctly in Arabic and CJK.
languages.custom: Pass languages to add or replace UI languages. Untranslated labels fall back to English. Override a few strings of an existing language with labels. The Arabic labels are exported as arabicLabels, a good starting point for another RTL language.
languages.display: When you show saved HTML, keep the dir attributes the editor wrote and wrap it in owe-content-root. Set lang on the container for content in another language so screen readers use the right voice.
